Reviewed exact head `ed19f0905781008d12275c6fbbff257cb77f044a`. **Changes required before merge:** one introduced cast regression is confirmed (inline comment). This is a bounded semantic review, not a full conformance or release approval.

Independent execution reproduced:
- Full `lake build`: 932 jobs passed (existing exact-head cache, checked by Lake; not a cache-free rebuild).
- RDF rdf-mt + SPARQL 1.1/1.2: 924 pass, zero failures/skips/unsupported.
- CSVW RDF and JSON: 270 pass each; JSON Schema draft-07: 770 pass.
- ShEx: 1,182 pass; SHACL Core full report comparison: 98 pass.
- Namespace manifests: 54 pass, three optional and two non-UTF8 excluded.
- RIF: 26 pass, one fail, 12 undecided; one unread and six import cases unattempted.
- XSLT subset: 84 pass, three attribute/namespace-order comparison failures, one missing-document refusal, as disclosed.
- All 17 Python regressions and seven additional RIF engine/saturation guards passed.

The RIF completeness propagation is a useful improvement: checked blocked/capped/unmappable cases do not supply a complete graph. The runner's zero exit status despite a decided failure is inherited and disclosed, but remains unsuitable as an exit-code-only release gate.

An additional **inherited** regex defect passes through the new ECMA profile:
```lean
#eval L4Factoidal.Regex.Profiles.matchWith .ecma2020 "^^a" "" "a"
-- Except.ok false
#eval L4Factoidal.JSONSchema.patternMatch "^^a" "a"
-- fail
```
Node RegExp returns true; `a$$` also fails on `a`. The older XPath engine encodes each anchor as a consuming sentinel. The new profile admits these patterns rather than refusing them. A finite 1,242-case differential corpus produced 1,067 agreements, 13 wrong decided answers (repeated anchors), and 162 refusals. Fix zero-width assertion handling or narrow admission; do not describe this as an introduced engine regression.

Methodology: `cast_target_valid` proves target membership, not source-to-target conversion correctness. Both wrong and right strings satisfy it. Preserve source datatype distinctions and add the actual canonical-conversion specification, caller regressions, and independent oracle/mutation tests.

The PR remains a development checkpoint. Its base has no merge base with main fetched at `0383de5280b361fb7638221212a108f23176d80b`. Do not retarget or replace main's files wholesale. Reconcile shared interfaces and main's existing functionality in smaller integrations, then test the exact packed public artifact. No Wasm/package validation or merge was performed in this review.

Detailed local record: `REVIEW-PR-1.md` with linked raw logs and reproducible Lean probes in the audit workspace.

comments.body:
**[P2] Preserve the source duration subtype when casting to string**

The new shared cast returns `"PT0S"` for `"P0M"^^xsd:yearMonthDuration`; it must return `"P0M"`. [F&O 2007 §17.1.2](https://www.w3.org/TR/2007/REC-xpath-functions-20070123/#casting-to-string) requires the source subtype's canonical form (§10.3.1.3 defines zero yearMonthDuration as P0M).

Executed against this exact head:
```lean
import L4Factoidal.RIF.Builtins
open L4Factoidal.RIF
#guard evalFunc "cast-string" [gLit "P0M" (xsdNs ++ "yearMonthDuration")] == some (gStr "P0M")
#guard evalFunc "cast-string" [gLit "P0Y" (xsdNs ++ "yearMonthDuration")] == some (gStr "P0M")
```
Both guards fail; actual results contain PT0S. The old cast fallback preserved P0M for the first input, so this is introduced.

The source projection erases the duration subtype before `stringValue`. Retain sufficient source-type information at the shared boundary, including derived string targets. Do not globally change zero-duration printing: dayTimeDuration zero and generic duration zero must still produce PT0S. Do not simply preserve input spelling: P0Y must canonicalize to P0M. Add both positive cases and those controls.

`cast_target_valid` cannot detect this: either output is a valid string.
